p-nakedandfamousdenim-14828081152365.d:
The MIJ19 Amaterasu Selvedge takes its name from Amaterasu, the sun goddess of Shinto mythology and the mythical ancestor of the Japanese Imperial Family. Her name, 天照 (Amaterasu), reflects both her identity and her role. Ama (天) means “heaven,” while terasu (照) means “to shine” or “to illuminate.” Together, they describe her divine duty to illuminate the heavens and bring light to the world. Amaterasu is revered as the highest-ranking kami in the Shinto pantheon, standing above the countless deities often referred to as the “eight million gods.”
Just as Amaterasu’s light illuminates the heavens, this fabric is defined by brightness and warmth. Woven in Japan from 11.5oz selvedge denim, the warp yarns are rope dyed with natural indigo, creating a soft, luminous shade of blue. The rope-dyeing process leaves the core of each warp yarn white, allowing the denim to develop a classic range of blue-to-white fades with wear.
A beige weft gives the reverse side of the fabric a warm, golden tone. Where the indigo warp wears through from abrasion, fraying, or rips, the beige yarns beneath may peek through, creating unexpected flashes of warmth against the fading blue.

p-nakedandfamousdenim-14984427995501.d:
The Galaxy Selvedge is a 13oz Japanese selvedge denim that blends cotton with rayon, using indigo rope-dyed warp yarns and a nep heavy weft to create a fabric with lively visual complexity. Nep, small clusters and knots of unmilled fiber, introduce organic irregularities into the weave, producing surface highlights and scattered texture that resemble star fields across the denim.
The addition of rayon in the weft softens the hand and enhances drape, giving Galaxy Selvedge a smoother, more fluid feel than a 100% cotton fabric of similar weight while maintaining depth and presence. When cuffed, the interaction between the nep accents and the interior weave becomes even more pronounced, revealing a more dramatic and playful texture on the inside.
